entities.summary:
Jean Buridan was a 14th-century French scholastic philosopher whose work significantly impacted the development of logic and epistemology.

Born in the late 13th century, Buridan studied at the University of Paris, where he became fascinated with the ideas of Aristotle and the works of William of Ockham.

Buridan's most notable contribution was his formulation of the Buridan's donkey problem, a thought experiment that explores the concept of causality and the nature of decision-making.

His work also influenced the development of medieval universities, particularly the University of Paris, where he became a prominent figure in the theological faculty.

Buridan's legacy extends beyond the realm of philosophy, as his ideas continue to shape our understanding of causality, free will, and the nature of reality.

The paradoxical implications of Buridan's donkey problem have captivated philosophers and scholars for centuries, making him one of the most enduring figures in the history of philosophy.
